title: Square isomorphism on bounded below derived categories
statement:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square],

$$
 \begin{array}{ccc}
 X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
 f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
 Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
 \end{array}
$$

with its specified isomorphism $\theta_\square:f'^{-1}g^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}g'^{-1}f^{-1}$ of functors $\Ab(Y_{\Et})\to\Ab(X'_{\Et})$, and let $f^{-1},g^{-1},f'^{-1},g'^{-1}$ also denote the inverse images on the bounded below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], each induced termwise through the localization functors $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The *derived square isomorphism*

$$
 \theta^D_\square:f'^{-1}\circ g^{-1}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }g'^{-1}\circ f^{-1}\qquad\text{of functors }\Dplus(Y_{\Et})\to\Dplus(X'_{\Et})
$$

is the unique natural isomorphism whose component at $QK^\bullet$, for every bounded below complex $K^\bullet$ of sheaves on $Y_{\Et}$, is, after the identifications $f'^{-1}g^{-1}QK^\bullet\cong Q(f'^{-1}g^{-1}K^\bullet)$ and $g'^{-1}f^{-1}QK^\bullet\cong Q(g'^{-1}f^{-1}K^\bullet)$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], the class $Q\bigl((\theta_{\square,K^r})_r\bigr)$ of the termwise isomorphism of complexes. (Existence and uniqueness: both composites are induced by the termwise composite functors on bounded below complexes, which invert quasi-isomorphisms, and a natural transformation between such functors descends uniquely along the localization; only the equality $fg'=gf'$ of the square enters $\theta_\square$.)
